title: A week with Fletcher Henderson at the Apollo
summary: Drummer Alphonso Steele got him a one-week Apollo job with Henderson's pick-up band from Chicago, whose book was easy compared with Henderson's famous hard arrangements.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Now, during the period that you were just gigging around, after you'd been with the bass player, John Kirby and with Billy Kyle's Sextet... You did some gigging. Tell me how you got with Fletcher Henderson for a week.
Well, I just told you.
Okay. Tell me for the tape.
Let me see. Where are going from? From Kirby? Is Kirby the last one?
Well, you were...

After I left Kirby, I was home, and let me see... I wasn't home all the time. Yeah, I was home this time, too. That when Steele came by the house. Yeah, that's right. I had finished with Kirby's band, and a friend of mine named Steele...
Alphonso Steele.
Alphonso Steele.
A drummer.
A drummer, that's right. He came by the
Holmes (12/5) - 60

house one morning, and asked me if I wanted to do a week in the theatre. I told him, "Yeah. I don't care. Who is it with?" And he told me, "Smack" -- the Fletcher Henderson Band. I said, "Is that right?" I was glad for that, you know; glad to get that. So he taken me to the theatre where they was rehearsing...
What theatre was that?
The Apollo Theatre.

And we go by the theatre where they were rehearsing, and talked to Smack, and he asked me could I make the week with him, and I told him, "Sure, why not?" Smack knew me from years before, you know. I mean, I wasn't no stranger to him. So there was no big deal, I mean, about it. Nothing... So okay, I was just hired on the moment, the spot of the moment, you know, and that was it. But it was only for the week in the theatre, that's all.
Was that a difficult book? Or what kind of a setup was that?
Well, I mean, he... I don't know, we didn't have too many numbers to play. It was four or five numbers that the band played. It wasn't all that difficult at that time.
Because Henderson was supposed to be famous for having a band that...
Holmes (12/5) - 61

Well, that's when he was arranging for his first band. That goes way back. And the band that he had after Louis went back to Chicago, Smack was doing his own writing then. That's when he had the tough arrangements.
And the weird keys.
Yeah. He wrote in all the unheard-of keys.
But this was nothing like that.

No, no. Everything was legible. It could be read. You could read the music. And it was in popular keys. So it was no... Well, I mean, after all, the caliber of the musicians he had in the band then were not the same as the ones that he had in his band. I mean, these were more or less a pick-up band of his from Chicago. I say a pick-up, because there was no... It was not a well-rehearsed band or anything like that. Mostly a pick-up band from Chicago. So he got moderate musicians, and he had moderate music for the book.
Was this a show? Was there dancing?
Oh yeah, it was regular...
Acts?

You know, in the theatre... They changed shows every week in the theatre, but they changed the bands, too. The bands are like the attraction, because they play for the show -- they play the whole show. Yeah, they
Holmes (12/5) - 62

changed the whole show every week. And the bands, they are the attraction -- most of the time. Unless somebody come in like Ella Fitzgerald or Pearl Bailey or something like that, then they were the attraction.
